questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain OSHA's mission and the purpose of the OSH Act
questions.keyword: OSHA mission and OSH Act purpose
questions.text: What is OSHA's main mission?

answers.text: To assure safe and healthful working conditions for workers by setting and enforcing standards and by providing training, outreach, education, and assistance
To guarantee that construction work has no hazards
To replace employer safety programs on construction sites
To provide workers' compensation benefits after an injury

explanations.a: OSHA's mission focuses on safe and healthful working conditions through standards, enforcement, training, outreach, education, and assistance. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Complaint-process clue: oSHA works to reduce hazards, but no agency can guarantee hazard-free construction work.
explanations.c: Outreach-limit clue: employers still have responsibility for workplace safety and health programs.
explanations.d: Safety context: workers' compensation is separate from OSHA's role in workplace safety and health.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain OSHA's mission and the purpose of the OSH Act
questions.keyword: OSHA mission and OSH Act purpose
questions.text: Why was the Occupational Safety and Health Act created?

answers.text: To make workers responsible for correcting all site hazards
To help ensure safe and healthful working conditions for workers
To approve every construction schedule before work begins
To remove the need for employers to train workers

explanations.a: Worker-protection clue: workers have responsibilities, but employers must provide safe and healthful workplaces.
explanations.b: The OSH Act was established to improve workplace safety and health protections for workers. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: OSHA-resource clue: oSHA does not approve every construction schedule before work starts.
explanations.d: Foundation recall: the OSH Act does not remove employer training responsibilities.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.1 Explain OSHA's mission and the purpose of the OSH Act
questions.keyword: OSHA mission and OSH Act purpose
questions.text: A construction worker is attending OSHA 10-Hour Construction training. A new construction worker asks why OSHA exists. Which answer is best?

answers.text: OSHA exists to certify every construction worker as competent
OSHA exists mainly to discipline workers after incidents
OSHA helps protect workers by setting and enforcing safety and health requirements and by providing education and assistance
OSHA exists to manage contractors' profit and project deadlines

explanations.a: Awareness-level check: oSHA Outreach training does not make every worker a competent person.
explanations.b: Responsibility boundary: oSHA focuses on workplace safety and health, not employee discipline.
explanations.c: This answer connects OSHA's role to worker protection, enforcement, and assistance. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Construction context: project cost and schedule management are not OSHA's mission.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: Which statement about worker rights is correct?

answers.text: Workers can ask OSHA to inspect a workplace if they believe serious hazards exist
Workers can be punished for asking about hazards
Workers must personally prove a violation before OSHA can receive a complaint
Workers lose OSHA rights if they are temporary or new

explanations.a: Workers may file complaints and request OSHA inspections when they believe workplace hazards exist. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Complaint-process clue: retaliation for exercising OSHA rights is prohibited.
explanations.c: Outreach-limit clue: workers can report concerns; OSHA determines how to evaluate the complaint.
explanations.d: Safety context: oSHA rights apply to covered workers regardless of being new or temporary.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: A crew member wants to see chemical hazard information for a product being used on site. Which right applies?

answers.text: The right to approve the product purchase contract
The right to access hazard information about materials and workplace hazards
The right to mix chemicals without instructions
The right to skip exposure controls if the task is short

explanations.a: Worker-protection clue: purchasing authority is not the worker right involved in hazard communication.
explanations.b: Workers must be able to receive information about hazards they may encounter. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: OSHA-resource clue: hazard information supports safe use; it does not permit unsafe mixing.
explanations.d: Foundation recall: short tasks can still require hazard controls.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: On site, a construction worker is attending OSHA 10-Hour Construction training. Which item is a worker right under OSHA?

answers.text: The right to remove guardrails without authorization
The right to decide which OSHA standards apply to the employer
The right to receive information and training about workplace hazards
The right to ignore site safety rules if work is urgent

explanations.a: Awareness-level check: removing protective systems can create fall hazards and is not a worker right.
explanations.b: Responsibility boundary: employers and OSHA determine compliance obligations; workers have rights to information, reporting, and protection.
explanations.c: Workers have a right to understand hazards and receive information and training in a language and vocabulary they can understand. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Construction context: workers still need to follow applicable safety and health rules.

questions.name: Introduction to OSHA
questions.objective: 1.2 Identify worker rights under OSHA
questions.text: A worker reports a suspected hazard to OSHA. What protection is most relevant?

answers.text: Permission to stop using required PPE
Automatic payment for the rest of the project
Authority to shut down the entire construction site alone
Protection from retaliation for exercising OSHA rights

explanations.a: Language clue: exercising OSHA rights does not remove the need to use required protective equipment.
explanations.b: Recognition clue: oSHA retaliation protection does not automatically provide project pay unrelated to the claim.
explanations.c: Course-scope clue: workers can report hazards, but site-wide shutdown authority is not simply created by a report.
explanations.d: Workers are protected from retaliation when they exercise OSHA rights such as reporting hazards or filing complaints. This is the correct answer.

questions.text: Which action is an example of exercising OSHA worker rights?

answers.text: Requesting copies of workplace injury and illness records that workers are allowed to access
Changing a scaffold design without approval
Refusing all safety training because OSHA exists
Disabling an alarm because it is distracting

explanations.b: Complaint-process clue: changing scaffold design is not a worker right and may create serious hazards.
explanations.c: Outreach-limit clue: workers should receive and participate in required safety training.
explanations.d: Safety context: disabling safety devices can increase risk and is not a protected worker right.
